PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-10-12
39M, general wellness examination.

S:
Patient presents for his yearly wellness visit. He reports feeling well overall and takes his blood pressure medication each morning, checking home readings twice a week. He works as a project manager, mostly seated, and cycles on weekends. Sister with schizophrenia. Appetite is good, weight stable, and sleep is about 7 hours most nights. He has good support at home and no new concerns today. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, occasional alcohol.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 68, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 180 lb, BMI 25.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): basic metabolic panel normal, lipid panel within goal, A1c 5.4%.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 122/76. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Family history: reviewed relevant family history with patient and discussed reassurance and routine follow-up.
3. Health maintenance: discussed age-appropriate preventive care and immunizations, which are up to date. Encouraged continued weekend cycling and adding light strength exercises twice weekly.
4. Lifestyle: reviewed balanced meals, limiting sodium, and taking regular breaks from prolonged sitting. Discussed consistent sleep and adequate hydration.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner as needed.
